mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is active whenever FEDFUNDS is below threshold.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% signals economic weakness, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicate strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS has increased from previous month.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 105.0 (INDPRO < 105.0) indicates a weakening supply chain, reducing corporate output and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1000.0 (HOUST > 1000.0) signal robust consumer demand, boosting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1000.0.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), strong job growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM) indicates economic recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPI (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicate aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS have increased from previous month.
